The paper is a **real publication**. The exact title is **“These issues aren't talked about at home”: a qualitative study of the sexual and reproductive health information preferences of adolescents in Vanuatu**—not “Are These Issues…”. It was published in **BMC Public Health in 2014** and is indexed as **PMID 25073619**. The searches and record retrieved here did not establish a DOI, so I can’t verify one.

**Methods and participants:** The study conducted 66 focus-group discussions with 341 male and female adolescents aged 15–19 in rural and urban communities on two Vanuatu islands, plus 12 interviews with policymakers and health-service providers. Researchers used inductive thematic analysis. The adolescent participants had a median age of 17; 48.7% were from rural areas.

**Findings:** Adolescents valued information about HIV and sexually transmitted infections but identified gaps in pregnancy prevention, condom use, puberty, sexuality, and relationships. They favored peer educators and health workers as trusted sources. Parents were not commonly consulted, though adolescents—particularly girls—said they would prefer them as sources despite sociocultural barriers. Schools and media were also identified as underused channels.

The search results identify a specific 2014 paper matching the subject, although the wording in the question differs from its published title. The reported methods and findings directly address adolescent SRH information preferences in Vanuatu.
